title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 269 (Omitted — sick companies / Chapter XIX)

content.overview: Section 269 was the last numbered provision of Chapter XIX (sections 253 to 269) on revival and rehabilitation of sick companies. That chapter has been omitted in full. Sick-company determination and revival under Chapter XIX are not current law. Corporate debt default and insolvency resolution for corporate persons are governed by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, before the National Company Law Tribunal as adjudicating authority.
content.glance: s. 269 omitted with Chapter XIX (last of sick-company revival block); not current procedure; use IBC for corporate insolvency and liquidation.
content.study: Section 269 closed Chapter XIX on revival and rehabilitation of sick companies. Sections 253 to 269 were omitted; they are not the current route for corporate distress. Current corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation of corporate persons is under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. A study answer that treats s. 269 as available current procedure is wrong. The topic is retained so the omitted number is not mistaken for a gap in the Act.

sections.heading: Omission
sections.body: Section 269 and Chapter XIX (ss. 253–269) on sick-company revival have been omitted and are not in force.

sections.heading: Current Law
sections.body: Corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation for debt default are under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, before the NCLT.

sections.heading: Study Note
sections.body: Do not plead omitted Chapter XIX as current procedure. Name the IBC route where corporate distress is in issue.

examples.title: Old reference
examples.body: A draft petition invoking s. 269 or Chapter XIX sick-company revival cannot be filed as current law.

examples.title: Current forum
examples.body: A financial creditor seeking resolution of corporate debt default proceeds under the IBC before the NCLT, not under omitted s. 269.

hypotheticals.question: Can a creditor still move under s. 269 for sick-company revival?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 269 and Chapter XIX have been omitted. Corporate insolvency is under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

distinctions.title: Omitted sick-company route (s. 269 / Chapter XIX) vs IBC
distinctions.left: Omitted Chapter XIX revival — not current law
distinctions.right: IBC corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation before NCLT

misconceptions.trap: Section 269 is still available for sick-company revival.
misconceptions.correction: Section 269 and Chapter XIX have been omitted. Debt default and corporate insolvency are under the IBC.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 269 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State that s. 269 / Chapter XIX is omitted. II. Name the IBC route. III. Conclude that the omitted section is not current procedure.
